Nintendo Is Staying Cautious on AI — and That Might Be the Smarter Move

thread // May 26, 2026 · Updated Sep 24, 2026

Read more on Threads

Is Nintendo being smart by staying cautious with generative AI, or is it falling behind?

While other companies rush into AI, Nintendo seems focused on protecting three things:

1. Copyright and IP
2. Game quality
3. Fan trust

Why Nintendo has more to lose than anybody

Nintendo's brand is built on polish and that "Nintendo magic." Mario, Zelda and Pokémon aren't just games. They're some of the most valuable characters in the world. So generative AI hits Nintendo from two directions.

First, protection. AI tools trained on the internet can spit out Nintendo-looking characters in seconds, and Nintendo has spent decades defending its IP harder than almost anyone.

Second, quality. Nintendo's reputation is that its games feel handmade and finished. If AI makes games feel cheap, risky or soulless, that damages the one thing Nintendo can't afford to lose.

Cautious isn't the same as anti-AI

I don't think Nintendo is anti-AI. I think it's being careful.

Games have used "AI" for decades: enemy behavior, pathfinding, how characters move around a level. That's not what people are arguing about. The debate is about generative AI: art, voices, writing and code made by models.

Nintendo can let everybody else find the problems first, then use whatever actually works.

Fan trust is the real currency

Gamers are quick to call out AI-generated art, voices and assets, and the backlash can overshadow an entire game. Nintendo fans trust that a Nintendo game was made with care. Staying cautious protects that trust, and that's worth more than whatever time AI might save.

Update (September 2026)

Nintendo's own words back this up. President Shuntaro Furukawa has said generative AI "can be used in creative ways" but that video games "cannot be created by technology alone," and that Nintendo will protect its intellectual property as AI laws develop around the world. This summer, Nintendo made it clear again that it will go after IP infringement whether AI is involved or not.

Not anti-AI. Careful. Exactly what I thought.

Sources: Game Developer, AUTOMATON, Nintendo Life

Quick answers

Does Nintendo use generative AI in its games? Nintendo hasn't said it does. President Shuntaro Furukawa has said the technology "can be used in creative ways," but that games "cannot be created by technology alone."

What is Nintendo's stance on AI? Open but careful: it's willing to consider creative uses, and it's focused on protecting its intellectual property as AI laws develop.

Has Nintendo used AI in games before? Yes, in the traditional sense, like systems that control how enemy characters move.

Your turn

Is Nintendo being smart, or falling behind? Tell me in the comments.
